title: Advisory committee annual reports and strategic plan progress
subtitle: Accessibility committee's 20th anniversary, 2025 Council schedule, park plans, staff well-being and community shout-outs
overview: Council spent most of the evening hearing annual reports from its advisory committees: sustainability, age-friendly, heritage, economic development, creative sector, Town and Gown, the Grand River Accessibility Advisory Committee (GRAAC) and the Waterloo Park Advisory Committee. The GRAAC report was paired with a recognition of the committee's 20th anniversary. Council received each of these reports for information, as it did the annual committee night report.

Staff also presented the first annual progress report on the 2023-2026 Strategic Plan, which Council received {{vote:m3}}. Staff described community conversations, a plan to track progress with two indicators per priority, and limited staff capacity. Council also approved the 2025 Council meeting schedule {{vote:m7}}, which sets the dates residents can plan around for meetings.

Council met in closed session before the public meeting. The minutes list labour relations, personal matters, solicitor-client advice and potential litigation as subjects, and report no decisions from it. In new business, members thanked community services staff for a large girls' hockey tournament, recognized a local martial arts club, and promoted a campaign against impaired driving.

decisions.detail: Council approved the proposed 2025 Council Meeting Schedule set out in Appendix A of report CORP2024-044.
Council received the 2023-2026 Strategic Plan progress report (CAO2024-026) as information.
Council received the Grand River Accessibility Advisory Committee's 2024 highlights report as information.
Council received the committee's November 2024 activity update (CTTEE2024-003) for information.
Council received the 2024 Committee Night Annual Report (CORP2024-043) as information.

debate: The sustainability committee's chair credited the city with progress, including the corporate climate action plan and added staff capacity. The chair said progress is far too slow against community and corporate targets, and urged clear public communication to keep support.

On the strategic plan, one councillor asked about staff well-being. Staff pointed to mental health supports, a wellness guide and an inclusion survey that showed demand for more support. Staff also reminded Council that capacity is limited and that taking on new priorities can mean delaying others.

GRAAC representatives raised concerns about accessible play equipment, a low share of affordable and accessible units in a non-profit housing project, and that the committee rarely learns the outcomes of projects it reviews. The mayor and councillors said they would look for a way to give feedback and suggested accessibility tours earlier in project design.

In discussing Town and Gown, a councillor asked about work on racism affecting international students. The committee chair said it was a serious concern and planned campus visits to hear from students. The chair also said the committee relies heavily on student volunteers and is trying to resource working groups properly.
The Waterloo Park Advisory Committee said it would finish ongoing projects and avoid steps that might pre-empt the park plan review planned for 2025.
